title: Density Operators and Quantum Noise
summary: Density operators, Kraus operators, and the difference between error probability and wrong-answer probability.
objectives: Write a Pauli error as Kraus operators and apply it to a density matrix
Read the probability of a wrong answer and the purity off a density matrix
Explain why an error in 40% of the runs does not mean a wrong answer in 40% of the runs
mission: An error that strikes in 40% of the runs does not spoil 40% of the answers, and this circuit shows it. H, T, T†, H returns |0⟩. Insert an error between T and T†: X with probability p_x, Z with probability p_z, nothing otherwise. Compute the final density matrix, and for p_x = p_z = 0.2 store in p_wrong the probability of measuring 1 and in purity the purity Tr(ρ²).

prediction.question: With p_x = p_z = 0.2, an error happens in 40% of the runs. In what fraction of the runs does the final measurement give 1?
options: 40%, since every error ends in a wrong result
20%, since only one of the two errors reaches the measurement
prediction.explanation: Z commutes with T and becomes X after the last H, so it always flips the result. X does not commute with T: it reaches the measurement as a rotation that gives 1 with probability 1/2. Total: 0.2 + 0.2 × 0.5 = 0.3.

hints: Ask what the error does to ρ: with probability p_x it applies X, with p_z it applies Z, otherwise nothing. Which three operators K, with which weights, give ρ → Σ K ρ K† with ΣK†K = I?

Return √(1 − p_x − p_z)·I, √p_x·X and √p_z·Z from error_kraus and apply them between the two T gates with qml.QubitChannel(error_kraus(p_x, p_z), wires=0). The circuit returns qml.density_matrix(wires=0) on the default.mixed device.
The probability of measuring 1 is the diagonal entry rho[1, 1], and the purity is np.trace(rho @ rho). Both come out with a zero imaginary part that np.real removes.

messages.ok: The density matrix is right for every error probability tested. The result is wrong in a fraction {p_wrong} of the runs, and the purity is {purity}: the noise left the qubit in a mixed state.
messages.no_circuit: Define the QNode circuit(p_x, p_z) on a default.mixed device.
messages.wrong_qubits: This lesson uses 1 qubit, but the circuit has {count}.
messages.no_noise: The final state is still pure, so the error never acts. Put qml.QubitChannel with the Kraus operators between T and T†.
messages.wrong_rho: With p_x = {px} and p_z = {pz} the probability of measuring 1 should be {want} and the circuit gives {got}. Either the error sits at the wrong place in the circuit, or the Kraus operators carry p where they need √p.
messages.missing: Store the result in the variable {name}.
messages.wrong_value: {name} is {actual}, which does not match the density matrix for p_x = p_z = 0.2. Read p_wrong from ρ[1, 1] and the purity from Tr(ρ²) of the final ρ.

challenge.mission: The mission's errors are Pauli mixtures, and they only shrink the Bloch vector toward the centre of the sphere. Energy loss does something else: a qubit in |1⟩ decays to |0⟩ with probability γ, and the Bloch vector moves toward |0⟩. Write damping_kraus(gamma), which returns the two Kraus operators of this amplitude damping channel, and a QNode damped(gamma) on a default.mixed device that prepares |+⟩ with a Hadamard gate and applies the channel with qml.QubitChannel. For γ = 0.36 store in bloch_plus the Bloch vector [x, y, z] of the result, in purity_plus its purity, and in z_from_mixed the z component of the output when the input is the maximally mixed state I/2. The validator checks that your operators satisfy ΣK†K = I, applies them to several states, and rebuilds the state from your QNode; any equivalent set of Kraus operators passes.
hints: Think of two things that can happen to a qubit that may lose energy: nothing, or a jump from |1⟩ to |0⟩. Each needs one operator, and the jump has amplitude √γ.

The no-jump operator must still account for the fact that not having jumped is evidence for |0⟩: it leaves |0⟩ alone and multiplies the amplitude of |1⟩ by √(1−γ). Then check that K0†K0 + K1†K1 is the identity, matrix by matrix.
The Bloch vector has components Tr(ρX), Tr(ρY) and Tr(ρZ). For I/2 a Pauli mixture gives z = 0; if your z_from_mixed is not 0, the channel is not one.

messages.ch_ok: The channel is complete and moves |+⟩ to the Bloch vector ({x}, 0, {z}) with purity {purity}. The z component is not zero, which no mixture of Pauli errors can produce from |+⟩.
messages.ch_kraus_format: damping_kraus({gamma}) must return a list of 2×2 matrices.
messages.ch_not_complete: For γ = {gamma} the sum of K†K has diagonal {diag} instead of 1, 1, so the trace of ρ would not stay 1. Check the factor on each operator: the amplitudes carry √, not the probabilities.
messages.ch_wrong_channel: For γ = {gamma} the channel gives ρ00 = {got} on one test state and it should give {want}. The operators are complete but do not describe decay: |1⟩ should go to |0⟩ with probability γ and |0⟩ should stay put.
messages.ch_no_qnode: Define the QNode damped(gamma) on a default.mixed device.
messages.ch_qnode_qubits: damped should use 1 qubit, but it uses {count}.
messages.ch_qnode_wrong: For γ = {gamma} the probability of 1 after H and the channel is {got} and it should be {want}. Check that the channel comes after the Hadamard gate and receives your operators for this γ.
messages.ch_missing: Store the result in the variable {name}.
messages.ch_wrong_value: {name} is {actual}, which does not match the output of the channel for |+⟩ with γ = 0.36. Rebuild it from the final ρ, using Tr(ρX), Tr(ρY), Tr(ρZ) for the Bloch vector.
